Hints: Apply the Vertical Line Test;A vertical line will only hit a horizontal line exactly once
Solution: A horizontal line (like y=3) passes the vertical line test. For every x, there is exactly one y.

Hints: Check if any x-value repeats;The input 1 goes to both 2 and 5

Solution: For any real number x, squaring it and adding 3 yields exactly one unique y-value. It is a parabola that passes the vertical line test.

Question Choices: Which defines a function? "Each x has exactly one y" "Each y has exactly one x"
Hints: The rule applies to the inputs (x);Outputs (y) can be repeated
Solution: The strict definition of a function is that every domain element (input x) maps to exactly one range element (output y).

Hints: The input 4 repeats, but it goes to the SAME output (5);There is no contradiction
Solution: The point (4,5) is just listed twice. The input 4 only ever maps to 5, so it is still a valid function.

Question Choices: Does this table represent a function? x: 1, 2, 3, 4; y: 5, 7, 9, 11 (Yes/No)
Hints: Check that no x repeats;All inputs are unique
Solution: Look at the x-values: 1, 2, 3, 4. None of them repeat, so each input has exactly one output.

Hints: If $x=9$, $y$ could be 3 or -3;One input yields two outputs
Solution: If you substitute x = 9, y could be 3 or -3 because (3)^2=9 and (-3)^2=9. One input gives two outputs.

Question Choices: Does a vertical line represent a function? (Yes/No)
Hints: Apply the Vertical Line Test;It hits all its own points simultaneously
Solution: A vertical line (like x=4) has infinite y-values for a single x-value. It fails the vertical line test.

Question Choices: Which is a function? "Student ID to Student Name" "Favorite Color to Student Name"
Hints: An ID belongs to exactly one student;A color can belong to many students
Solution: One ID belongs to exactly one student (Function). However, one color can belong to multiple students (Not a function).

Question Choices: Which represents a function? "Day of the week to Temperature" "Temperature to Day of the week"
Hints: A day only has one official high temperature;But multiple days can have the exact same temperature
Solution: Each specific day can only have one recorded high temperature. Multiple days can have the same temperature, making the reverse untrue.
